chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

There are four prayers which a man prays at any time: a missed prayer which you make up whenever you remember it; the two units of the obligatory circumambulation prayer; the eclipse prayer; and the funeral prayer. These are the prayers which a man may pray at all times.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: Two units of the obligatory circumambulation prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the four prayers that can be performed at any time in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delineates four specific prayers exempt from the general prohibition of *salat al-fadli* (supererogatory prayers) during forbidden times (*awqat al-karahah*). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the performance of these acts—making up missed prayers, tawaf prayer, eclipse prayer, and funeral prayer—regardless of the time, thereby emphasizing the priority of fulfilling communal and individual obligations over temporal restrictions.
